sentences.text: Lautropia mirabilis is a Gram-negative coccoid bacterium that has been isolated from oral and upper respiratory sites.
It is described as a facultative anaerobic coccus detected mainly at respiratory sites in immunodeficient patients with HIV or cystic fibrosis.
Published reports describe its pathogenic potential as unclear, with knowledge limited by the small number of documented cases.
One report describes sepsis with this organism in a 39-year-old woman with common variable immunodeficiency, in whom active periodontitis was observed as the origin.
A study in Shanghai and Guangxi isolated 38 strains from sputum or bronchoalveolar lavage specimens, and reported that the majority of those patients had underlying diseases.
